title: EDC probing: In-cell mapping of G and U base-pairing interactions
key_innovation: Compared with DMS, which primarily interrogates adenine and cytosine, EDC expands nucleotide-specific probing to guanine and uracil residues and enables analysis of RNA base-pairing states in living cells.

blocks.text: How does EDC enable G/U-specific RNA structure probing inside cells?

blocks.alt: Development of EDC as an in-cell RNA structure probe
blocks.legend: **Figure 1. Development of EDC as an in-cell RNA structure probe.** EDC is a membrane-permeable carbodiimide reagent that selectively modifies accessible guanine and uracil residues. Following reverse transcription, modification sites are detected to generate nucleotide-resolution RNA structure profiles. This approach extends chemical probing beyond DMS-accessible adenine and cytosine residues.
blocks.label: EDC probing F1

blocks.text: How can EDC complement DMS to improve RNA structure determination?

blocks.alt: Combining EDC and DMS reveals complementary RNA structural information
blocks.legend: **Figure 2. Combining EDC and DMS reveals complementary RNA structural information.** EDC and DMS provide complementary nucleotide-specific information by interrogating different Watson–Crick faces. Integration of both datasets improves secondary structure modeling of cellular RNAs, including structured regions within long noncoding RNAs.
blocks.label: EDC probing F2
